guide.description: grep scans a file (or stdin) line by line and prints every line matching a pattern. It's the tool you reach for first when you need to find something inside text — a log line, a config value, a name in a list.

flags.desc: invert the match — print lines that DON'T match
print a count of matching lines instead of the lines themselves
prefix each match with its line number

examples.note: -c collapses the matches to a single count

exercises.title: Filter lines with grep
exercises.task: Print every line in access.log containing '404'.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: No flags needed here — just the pattern and the file

exercises.title: Count matches with -c
exercises.task: Instead of printing the matching lines, print how many lines contain '200' using -c.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: -c makes grep print a count instead of the matching lines
The flag goes right after grep, before the pattern

criteria.label: Print the count of 200 lines, not the lines

exercises.title: Invert the match with -v
exercises.task: Print every line that does NOT contain '200', using -v.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: -v inverts the match — it prints lines that DON'T match
Same pattern as before, just add the -v flag
